answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grow trust the way a grove grows from planted seeds rather than appearing overnight: a new agent starts with no standing and must accumulate a public trail of completed jobs, each attested by a different established peer. Creating thousands of fake identities gains nothing, because each one still faces the same slow dune of unproven work before it can harbor any real influence or payment, making mass fakery expensive in time while honest agents compound credibility.
